newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore opposition lodges formal poll complaint.
newsitem.headline: Singapore opposition lodges formal poll complaint.

text.p: Singapore's opposition Workers' Party said on Monday it had complained to police, claiming that Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong had infringed election rules during polling last week.
Goh has already denied doing anything wrong during voting in the key Cheng San constituency last Thursday, which his People's Action Party (PAP) won with 54 percent of the vote.
Overall, the PAP won 65 percent of the vote as it halved the opposition presence in parliament to just two seats, but its win in Cheng San left the Workers' Party bitter.
"A complaint has been made to the Ang Mo Kio Police Division and the party will wait to see what action the police propose to take," the Workers' Party said in a statement.
It claimed that Goh and two deputy prime ministers entered polling stations in multi-member Cheng San, where the Workers' Party was widely thought to have its best chance of winning.
Victory there would have given it five seats in parliament in a winner-take-all contest and Goh threw all the PAP's heavy weapons into the battle to prevent that.
The Workers' Party statement argued that election rules banned candidates from entering a polling centre or waiting within 200 metres (yards) of one during voting.
Police confirmed they had received the complaint and said they were studying it.
Goh said at the weekend that although he visited different polling stations, he was never inside.
"Nobody has ever accused the PAP of stuffing ballot boxes," he said.
The Workers' Party also claimed there had been threats to the life of Tang Liang Hong, one of the five party candidates in Cheng San who was the focus of the PAP campaign.
Goh accused Tang of being a "Chinese chauvinist" who was a danger to multi-ethnic Singapore, where the population is 77 percent ethnic Chinese with significant minorities of Malays and Indians.
Tang and his daughter had been the target of threats following Goh's accusations, the Workers' Party statement said.

"It appears there is even a threat to his life. What is this country coming to? Are opposition politicians to live in fear and danger to their life or of physical injury as in some other countries?" it said.
Tang has made formal complaints to police about the alleged threats. Police said on Monday they were studying the complaints.
The Straits Times newspaper said on Monday that Tang, a lawyer, had crossed the border into Malaysia because he feared for his safety in Singapore.
